lots.what_it_is: Textured resin tiger head bust on a rock base (catalogued as LION HEAD ORNAMENT), in the style of Edge Sculpture but not the Edge Tiger Bust design
lots.guide_summary: Nothing survives: no SOLD, UNSOLD or ASKING evidence. WebSearch budget was used up for both the researcher and the verifier, so no price evidence could be gathered. The official Edge Sculpture Tiger Bust page (edgesculpture.com/tiger_bust, page opened, no price shown) was used only to check the identification, and it does not match this lot.
lots.working: No SOLD evidence, so keep_max_hammer = 0 and flip_max_hammer = 0. Gowans premium 19.8% (all-in = hammer x 1.198) would apply.
lots.confidence_reason: Single front photo, no maker mark legible, no price evidence of any kind.
lots.dropped_entries: Researcher had no entries. Researcher's Edge Sculpture Tiger Bust Jungle Hunter reference was not a price and is a different item. I compared the lot with the official Edge EDB31 Tiger Bust (edgesculpture.com/tiger_bust, page opened, 400mm high, orange, white and black faceted finish, no base, closed mouth). The lot has a rock base, an open mouth with fangs, a pitted all-over brown finish and different sculpting, so it is not the Edge EDB31 and not the Jungle Hunter. It reads as a generic Edge-inspired homewares ornament.
lots.key_photo_findings: One photo only. Face is a tiger (not a lion as catalogued): rounded ears, striped forehead ridges, yellow-green eyes, open mouth with yellow fangs, sitting on a moulded rock base. Pitted stone-like texture painted in brown and ochre. The white oval at the top of the head is a sticker (enlarged; lettering not legible), likely a retailer or maker label rather than a reflection. Design and base differ from the official Edge Sculpture Tiger Bust, so treat as an imitation or generic decor piece.
lots.condition: No chips or breaks visible from the front; back and underside not shown.
lots.question_for_gowans: What does the white oval sticker on top of the head say, and is there any maker name or Edge Sculpture mark on the underside or back? What is the height?

Correction to the researcher's identification: the red plane is a Stanley Surform (label 'STANLEY SURFORM' read on enlargement), a common tool, and '1998' is a white inventory tag like the 1762, 1764 and 1658 tags on other planes, not a date.
lots.key_photo_findings: Enlarged crops. Red plane reads STANLEY SURFORM with a 1998 tag, paint wear. Black plane with green adjuster and brass thumbscrew has a handwritten tag 'MODEL MAKING PLANE B/S' (or 8/5); a grey cast plane carries the same tag. Three small rosewood bodied planes with brass thumbscrews and steel irons (tags 1762, 1764 and one untagged) look like modern hobby miniature planes rather than antique infills. Green painted cast plane has heavy paint loss and rust. Numbered tags suggest a collector's inventory. No maker marks legible on the small cast or wooden planes.
lots.condition: Mixed: user wear, paint loss and some rust on the cast planes; wooden miniatures look clean.
lots.question_for_gowans: Are there any maker names on the small cast planes or the rosewood miniatures (soles, irons or lever caps), and are all irons and screws present?
